how_to_use: The Data Model Gallery. Each cloud has a category page (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/data-models/guide/<cloud>-category.html; for example manufacturing-cloud-category.html) listing one guide per capability; each guide has an intro sentence; the list of entities it includes and an ERD image. Use the guides as the source capabilities. Entities shared by many guides (Account; Contact; Product; User; Period; Location) are hubs.

Example for Manufacturing Cloud: each industry cloud has an API developer guide whose Standard Objects section lists every object with its API name; each object page starts with a one-line description ('Represents ...') and lists its fields: reference fields with 'Refers To' and sometimes 'Lookup'; picklist values in alphabetical order. Find the guide for another cloud by searching '<cloud> developer guide standard objects site:developer.salesforce.com'.
The core Object Reference: every standard object of Sales; Service and the platform; with descriptions and fields.

Salesforce Help has a feature article per capability (for example sf.mfg_warranties_parent.htm). Search 'site:help.salesforce.com <cloud> <capability>' and link the article that explains how to use the capability; title the link 'How to? (Salesforce help)'.
Table (entity) reference for Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement apps; each app (Sales; Customer Service; Field Service) has its own table list. Tables are not grouped by capability; infer the grouping.

Understanding the CRM: the standard objects (contacts; companies; deals; tickets and so on) and how associations link them. Each object has its own API guide with its properties. Not grouped by capability; infer the grouping from the hubs.
No single public table list. Search the product documentation for 'tables installed with <application>' and the Common Service Data Model (CSDM); record what could not be found as a gap.
